{"id": "be1de9c6-78d4-4ddf-9b07-80c9dd9f6b8f", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Why are my Lambda functions in eu-central-1 slow on the first request after a quiet period?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "2151df50-c374-4d28-baed-d944279a59ab", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "This is the classic Lambda **cold start** pattern — here's what's happening:

**What causes it:**
- When a function hasn't been invoked for a while, Lambda reclaims the execution environment (the container running your code).
- The next request has to spin up a fresh environment from scratch: download/mount your code package, start the runtime (Node, Python, Java, etc.), and run any top-level initialization code (DB connections, SDK clients, config loading) before your handler even starts.
- This "init" phase adds latency on top of normal execution time — often tens of milliseconds for small functions, but it can run into seconds for larger packages, VPC-attached functions, or runtimes like Java/.NET with heavier startup costs.

**Factors that make it worse:**
- **VPC attachment** — ENI setup used to add significant delay; it's much better now with Hyperplane ENIs, but still adds some overhead.
- **Package/image size** — larger deployment packages or container images take longer to load.
- **Runtime** — JVM-based and .NET functions generally have slower cold starts than Python/Node/Go.
- **Heavy init code** — SDK client setup, loading large dependencies, or fetching secrets/config at startup all run during the cold init.
- **Low traffic / sporadic invocations** — if nothing's invoking the function for stretches of time, Lambda scales environments down to zero, so every "wake up" pays the cold start cost. This matches your "after a quiet period" observation exactly.

**Common fixes:**
- **Provisioned Concurrency** — keeps a set number of environments warm, eliminating cold starts for that capacity.
- **SnapStart** (Java) — caches a post-init snapshot to skip re-running init code.
- Trim deployment package size and move non-essential work out of the init path.
- Avoid unnecessary VPC attachment if the function doesn't need it.

If you want, I can pull the actual Init Duration / cold start metrics for your functions in eu-central-1 to see which ones are affected and by how much — that'd tell us whether Provisioned Concurrency is worth it for specific functions.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
